html:
After the fall of Anuradhapura, the Sinhalese kings of Sri Lanka ruled from a line of later capitals for almost eight hundred years, until the British took the last one in 1815.

  • Polonnaruwa, 1055 to about 1232. Vijayabahu I drove the Cholas off the island by 1070. Parakramabahu I built its great reservoirs and Buddha statues. An invader from India, Magha, wrecked it in 1215.
  • The move south-west. The kings left the dry zone, and its reservoirs silted up and the jungle and malaria took it. Capitals followed one another at Dambadeniya, Yapahuwa, Kurunegala and Gampola. A Tamil kingdom grew up at Jaffna in the north.
  • Kotte, 1412 to 1597, near modern Colombo. It lived on cinnamon. The Portuguese arrived in 1505 and within a century controlled the coast (see Ceylon).
  • Kandy, about 1469 to 1815, in the central hills. It fought off the Portuguese and the Dutch for two centuries. Its own chiefs handed it to the British in 1815.

Wherever the king went, the tooth relic of the Buddha went with him, since holding it was the sign of the right to rule. It rests in Kandy today (see the Temple of the Tooth).
sum: After the fall of Anuradhapura, the Sinhalese kings of Sri Lanka ruled from a line of later capitals for almost eight hundred years, until the British took the last one in 1815.
